title: Fishing Gear Technology
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned 200L Fishing Gear Technology curriculum: classification of fishing gear (nets, hooks and lines, traps), gear construction terms (mesh size, twine, floats/sinkers), major gear types (gillnets, seine nets, trawl nets, cast nets, longlines), gear selectivity, fishing craft, gear materials, and traditional Nigerian fishing methods.

questions.question: Fishing gear technology is primarily concerned with the study of:
options: The design, construction, and operation of equipment used to capture aquatic organisms
The nutritional requirements of farmed fish
The genetics of wild fish populations
The chemistry of fish preservation
questions.correct_answer: The design, construction, and operation of equipment used to capture aquatic organisms
questions.explanation: Fishing gear technology covers the engineering and operational principles behind nets, hooks, traps, and other devices used to harvest fish and other aquatic organisms.

questions.question: Fishing gears are broadly classified based on their:
options: Design, construction material, and method of operation
Colour only
Country of manufacture only
Selling price only
questions.correct_answer: Design, construction material, and method of operation
questions.explanation: Fishing gear classification systems (such as the FAO ISSCFG) group gears based on structural design and the principle by which they capture fish, such as netting, hooking, or trapping.

questions.question: A gillnet captures fish primarily by:
options: Entangling the fish's gills or body as it tries to swim through the net mesh
Trapping fish inside an enclosed cage with no way in or out
Attracting fish with a baited hook
Using an electric current to stun fish
questions.correct_answer: Entangling the fish's gills or body as it tries to swim through the net mesh
questions.explanation: Gillnets are designed with mesh sized so that a fish's head passes through but its body is too large, causing the netting to snag behind the gill covers as the fish tries to back out.

questions.question: Mesh size selectivity in gillnets means that:
options: Different mesh sizes tend to capture fish of particular size ranges, allowing smaller and larger fish to escape
All fish regardless of size are captured equally by any mesh size
Mesh size has no relationship to the size of fish captured
Larger mesh always catches smaller fish than smaller mesh
questions.correct_answer: Different mesh sizes tend to capture fish of particular size ranges, allowing smaller and larger fish to escape
questions.explanation: Gillnet mesh size determines which fish sizes are most likely to be caught: fish too small pass through the mesh entirely, while fish too large cannot enter, giving gillnets inherent size selectivity.

questions.question: A seine net is generally operated by:
options: Encircling a school of fish and then drawing the net closed or hauling it to shore
Being left stationary on the seabed for days at a time
Using baited hooks along a long line
Attracting fish with a light source only, without any net
questions.correct_answer: Encircling a school of fish and then drawing the net closed or hauling it to shore
questions.explanation: Seine nets are actively deployed to surround fish schools, after which the net is hauled in, either onto a beach (beach seine) or aboard a vessel (purse seine), concentrating and capturing the fish.

questions.question: A purse seine differs from a simple beach seine mainly in that a purse seine:
options: Has a drawstring (purse line) at the bottom that closes the net into a bag shape, preventing fish from escaping downward
Is operated exclusively from the shore by hand
Has no bottom line of any kind
Is used only for freshwater ponds
questions.correct_answer: Has a drawstring (purse line) at the bottom that closes the net into a bag shape, preventing fish from escaping downward
questions.explanation: The purse line running through rings along the net's bottom edge can be pulled to cinch the net closed like a purse, trapping the encircled fish and preventing them from diving beneath the net to escape.

questions.question: A trawl net is a fishing gear that is:
options: Towed through the water or along the seabed by a moving vessel to capture fish
Left completely stationary and never moved once set
Operated exclusively by hand-casting from the shore
Used only to catch fish using bait on hooks
questions.correct_answer: Towed through the water or along the seabed by a moving vessel to capture fish
questions.explanation: Trawl nets are actively towed behind a moving boat, either near the bottom (bottom trawl) or in midwater (pelagic trawl), to capture fish and other organisms in their path.

questions.question: 'Otter boards' attached to a bottom trawl net function to:
options: Spread the mouth of the net horizontally open as it is towed through the water
Anchor the net permanently to one spot on the seabed
Attract fish visually toward the net
Measure the depth of the water
questions.correct_answer: Spread the mouth of the net horizontally open as it is towed through the water
questions.explanation: Otter boards (trawl doors) use hydrodynamic forces created by water flow to spread apart and hold the net mouth open horizontally while being towed, maximizing the area swept.

questions.question: A cast net is typically operated by:
options: A single fisher throwing the net by hand so it spreads into a circular shape over the water before sinking and being retrieved
A large vessel towing it for hours at sea
Setting it stationary underwater for several days without checking
Using a mechanical winch operated from a factory ship
questions.correct_answer: A single fisher throwing the net by hand so it spreads into a circular shape over the water before sinking and being retrieved
questions.explanation: Cast nets are weighted circular nets thrown by hand over shallow water or schools of fish, sinking to trap fish beneath before being gathered and hauled in by the fisher.

questions.question: A longline fishing gear consists of:
options: A long main line with numerous baited hooks attached at intervals via shorter branch lines
A single net with no hooks at all
A trap made entirely of woven bamboo
An electrified cable used to stun fish
questions.correct_answer: A long main line with numerous baited hooks attached at intervals via shorter branch lines
questions.explanation: Longlines consist of a main horizontal line, which can extend for kilometres, with baited hooks attached at intervals via shorter snoods or branch lines, targeting fish that take the bait.

questions.question: A handline, one of the simplest hook-and-line gears, is characterized by:
options: A single fishing line with one or a few hooks, operated directly by hand
Thousands of hooks spread over many kilometres
A large net with no hooks
An automated hydraulic hauling system only used on trawlers
questions.correct_answer: A single fishing line with one or a few hooks, operated directly by hand
questions.explanation: Handlines are simple, low-technology gear consisting of a line with one or a few hooks, commonly used by individual artisanal fishers without mechanized equipment.

questions.question: Fish traps (e.g. basket traps, pots) capture fish primarily by:
options: Luring or guiding fish into an enclosed structure from which escape is difficult
Directly entangling fish gills in netting mesh
Using baited hooks that pierce the fish's mouth
Stunning fish with an electric current
questions.correct_answer: Luring or guiding fish into an enclosed structure from which escape is difficult
questions.explanation: Traps rely on a funnel-shaped entrance or similar design that allows fish to enter easily (often attracted by bait) but makes it difficult for them to find their way back out.

questions.question: The traditional 'Malaka' or woven basket trap used in Nigerian artisanal fisheries is typically made from:
options: Locally available plant materials such as bamboo or raffia
Stainless steel wire only
Synthetic plastic exclusively
Reinforced concrete
questions.correct_answer: Locally available plant materials such as bamboo or raffia
questions.explanation: Traditional Nigerian basket traps are typically hand-woven from local plant fibres such as bamboo, raffia palm, or cane, reflecting indigenous low-cost gear construction methods.

questions.question: In gear construction, 'mesh size' generally refers to:
options: The distance between two opposite knots of a stretched mesh in a net
The total weight of the entire net
The colour of the netting material
The length of the net from end to end
questions.correct_answer: The distance between two opposite knots of a stretched mesh in a net
questions.explanation: Mesh size is a standardized measurement of the netting's opening, typically taken as the distance between opposite knots when the mesh is fully stretched, directly affecting gear selectivity.

questions.question: 'Twine' in fishing net construction refers to:
options: The thread or cord material from which the netting is woven or knotted
The float attached to the top of the net
The weight attached to the bottom of the net
The boat used to deploy the net
questions.correct_answer: The thread or cord material from which the netting is woven or knotted
questions.explanation: Twine is the basic thread material, whether natural fibre or synthetic, used to knot or weave together the meshes that make up a fishing net.

questions.question: Floats attached to the headline (top edge) of a fishing net primarily function to:
options: Keep the top of the net buoyant and properly positioned in the water column
Add extra weight to sink the net to the seabed
Attract fish visually toward the net
Measure the depth of the water
questions.correct_answer: Keep the top of the net buoyant and properly positioned in the water column
questions.explanation: Floats provide buoyancy along the headline, helping the net maintain its vertical spread and correct orientation in the water, working opposite to the sinkers on the footline.

questions.question: Sinkers (leads) attached to the footline (bottom edge) of a net primarily function to:
options: Weigh down the bottom of the net so it hangs vertically or reaches the desired depth
Keep the entire net floating at the surface
Increase the net's colour visibility to fish
Repel predators from approaching the net
questions.correct_answer: Weigh down the bottom of the net so it hangs vertically or reaches the desired depth
questions.explanation: Sinkers counterbalance the floats on the headline, ensuring the net hangs properly in the water column or sinks appropriately to fish the target depth.

questions.question: Modern fishing nets are predominantly constructed from which type of material, replacing older natural fibres?
options: Synthetic fibres such as nylon and polyethylene
Cotton exclusively
Raw animal hide
Unprocessed plant bark only
questions.correct_answer: Synthetic fibres such as nylon and polyethylene
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres like nylon and polyethylene have largely replaced natural fibres (cotton, hemp) in modern net construction due to their greater strength, durability, and resistance to rot.

questions.question: A key advantage of synthetic (e.g. nylon) netting material over traditional natural fibre netting is:
options: Greater resistance to rotting, higher strength-to-weight ratio, and longer service life
Much higher cost with no performance benefit
Complete biodegradability within days
Inability to be dyed or coloured
questions.correct_answer: Greater resistance to rotting, higher strength-to-weight ratio, and longer service life
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres resist microbial decay and abrasion far better than natural fibres like cotton or hemp, while also being lighter and stronger for a given thickness, extending gear lifespan.

questions.question: Gear selectivity in fisheries management refers to:
options: The ability of a fishing gear to catch fish of a certain size, species, or age while allowing others to escape
The total weight of fish a gear can hold at once
The colour of the netting used
The price a fisher pays for the gear
questions.correct_answer: The ability of a fishing gear to catch fish of a certain size, species, or age while allowing others to escape
questions.explanation: Selectivity describes how a gear's design (e.g. mesh size, hook size) determines which sizes or species of fish are captured, an important consideration for sustainable fisheries management.

questions.question: Using an excessively small mesh size in gillnets or seine nets is discouraged in fisheries management mainly because it:
options: Captures large numbers of small, immature fish, threatening future stock recruitment
Only catches fish that are already too old to reproduce
Has no impact on fish population sustainability
Increases the market value of the catch
questions.correct_answer: Captures large numbers of small, immature fish, threatening future stock recruitment
questions.explanation: Small mesh sizes indiscriminately capture juvenile, immature fish before they can reproduce, undermining recruitment and long-term sustainability of the fish stock, which is why minimum mesh size regulations exist.

questions.question: Which of the following fishing methods is generally considered the most environmentally destructive due to high bycatch and habitat damage?
options: Bottom trawling over sensitive seabed habitats
Selective handline fishing
Traditional basket trapping
Small-scale cast netting
questions.correct_answer: Bottom trawling over sensitive seabed habitats
questions.explanation: Bottom trawling drags heavy gear across the seafloor, often damaging benthic habitats and capturing substantial non-target bycatch, making it one of the more environmentally impactful fishing methods compared to selective, low-impact gears.

questions.question: The 'dug-out canoe', a traditional fishing craft widely used across Nigerian inland and coastal waters, is typically constructed by:
options: Carving and hollowing out a single large log
Welding together multiple sheets of steel
Moulding fiberglass around a wooden frame
Assembling inflatable rubber sections
questions.correct_answer: Carving and hollowing out a single large log
questions.explanation: Dug-out canoes are traditionally made by hollowing a single tree trunk into a boat shape, a technique long used by Nigerian artisanal fishing communities.

questions.question: An outboard engine attached to an artisanal fishing canoe primarily provides which advantage over paddling alone?
options: Greater speed and range, allowing fishers to reach more distant fishing grounds
Automatic identification of fish species
Elimination of the need for any fishing gear
Automatic mesh size adjustment
questions.correct_answer: Greater speed and range, allowing fishers to reach more distant fishing grounds
questions.explanation: Motorization significantly increases a fishing craft's speed and operational range compared to manual paddling, enabling access to more distant or productive fishing grounds and reducing time at sea.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'active' fishing gear, as opposed to 'passive' fishing gear?
options: Gear that is actively moved or towed to pursue and capture fish, such as a trawl net
Gear that is left stationary and waits for fish to encounter it
Gear that requires no human operation at all
Gear used only in aquaculture ponds
questions.correct_answer: Gear that is actively moved or towed to pursue and capture fish, such as a trawl net
questions.explanation: Active gears, like trawls and seines, are moved through the water to encircle or overtake fish, in contrast to passive gears such as gillnets and traps that remain stationary while fish encounter them.

questions.question: Passive fishing gear, such as a stationary gillnet or fish trap, operates by:
options: Remaining largely stationary while fish swim into or become caught by it
Being continuously towed through open water
Requiring the vessel to move at high speed at all times
Using an electric current to actively chase fish
questions.correct_answer: Remaining largely stationary while fish swim into or become caught by it
questions.explanation: Passive gears rely on the natural movement of fish encountering the stationary gear (e.g. swimming into a net or trap), rather than the gear actively pursuing the fish.

questions.question: A cast net's effectiveness depends heavily on the skill of the fisher mainly because it must be:
options: Thrown with a specific technique so it opens into a full circular spread before sinking
Left in the water for several weeks without checking
Attached permanently to a fixed post on the riverbank
Powered by an electric motor to open automatically
questions.correct_answer: Thrown with a specific technique so it opens into a full circular spread before sinking
questions.explanation: Proper casting technique is essential for the net to open fully into its circular shape as it lands on the water, maximizing the area covered and the chance of trapping fish beneath it.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an 'entangling' gear, distinct from encircling or trapping gears?
options: A gillnet, which snags fish by their gills or body as they try to pass through the mesh
A purse seine, which encircles a school before closing
A basket trap, which lures fish into an enclosed chamber
A dredge, which is dragged along the bottom to collect molluscs
questions.correct_answer: A gillnet, which snags fish by their gills or body as they try to pass through the mesh
questions.explanation: Entangling gears, primarily gillnets and trammel nets, capture fish by physically snagging or enmeshing them in netting, distinct from the encircling action of seines or the luring action of traps.

questions.question: A trammel net differs from a standard single-panel gillnet in that it consists of:
options: Three layers of netting (two outer panels of large mesh flanking an inner panel of smaller, looser mesh)
A single panel of extremely fine mesh only
No netting at all, using only hooks
A rigid metal frame instead of flexible netting
questions.correct_answer: Three layers of netting (two outer panels of large mesh flanking an inner panel of smaller, looser mesh)
questions.explanation: Trammel nets use a three-layer construction where fish push the loose inner panel through the larger outer mesh, forming a pocket that traps the fish, increasing catch efficiency compared to a single gillnet panel.

questions.question: The use of poison or explosives in fishing is widely prohibited in fisheries regulations mainly because it:
options: Indiscriminately kills fish of all sizes and damages the aquatic habitat
Only harms the largest fish while sparing all juveniles
Improves the long-term sustainability of fish stocks
Increases gear selectivity dramatically
questions.correct_answer: Indiscriminately kills fish of all sizes and damages the aquatic habitat
questions.explanation: Destructive fishing methods like poisoning and blast fishing kill fish and other organisms indiscriminately regardless of size or species, and often cause severe, lasting damage to aquatic habitats, which is why they are banned.
